statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-54787 (GHSA-wqqc-jjcq-vfxm, GO-2026-6162): before sigstore-go 1.2.1, verifying a bundle signed with a self-managed long-lived key (an ExpiringKey without a certificate) does not check the signing timestamp against the key's validity window, so someone holding expired key material can sign bundles that are still accepted: https://github.com/sigstore/sigstore-go/security/advisories/GHSA-wqqc-jjcq-vfxm. It is fixed in 1.2.1 by https://github.com/sigstore/sigstore-go/commit/4594ab4c779d08be1f4419803a8249188f35ed5f (pull request 642), whose only non-test change adds the check to (*Verifier).Verify in pkg/verify/signed_entity.go. The Go vulnerability database lists no affected symbols for this entry, so we searched for that function and for NewVerifier, which creates the Verifier. The vulnerable code is not in this package. We downloaded every package built from the trivy and trivy-fips sources in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository: trivy and trivy-dev from the main repository and trivy-fips and trivy-fips-dev from the security repository, each 0.69.1-r0 through the current 0.74.0-r12 (38 builds), for x86_64 and aarch64, 304 package files, each checked against its repository index checksum and data hash. Each holds one file, /usr/bin/trivy, a statically linked Go program built with GOOS=linux and CGO_ENABLED=0 that keeps its symbol table; its only module replacement, in 0.69.1-r0 to 0.69.3-r7, is for github.com/opencontainers/runtime-spec. We read the symbol table of every build with go tool nm and searched the bytes of every binary. The build information lists github.com/sigstore/sigstore-go v1.1.4 in 0.69.1-r0 to 0.71.2-r2 and v1.2.1 in 0.71.2-r3; later builds do not include the module. The only sigstore-go functions in any build are the package initializers bundle.init and verify.init, in the builds that list the module; no build has (*Verifier).Verify or NewVerifier. The byte search finds neither sigstore-go/pkg/verify.(*Verifier).Verify nor sigstore-go/pkg/verify.NewVerifier in any binary, and the only sigstore-go source files it finds named are pkg/bundle/bundle.go and pkg/verify/tlog.go, not signed_entity.go. runtime.main is in every build. As a positive control, we built a program against sigstore-go v1.1.4 that creates a Verifier with NewVerifier and calls Verify, for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 with CGO_ENABLED=0: go tool nm finds verify.NewVerifier and verify.(*Verifier).Verify in both, and the byte search finds sigstore-go/pkg/verify.(*Verifier).Verify in both.
